sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Carver County?
sections.html:
Two Carver County offices share the work, and both sit at 600 East 4th Street in Chaska. Billing and payments go through Property Tax at (952) 361-1910 or custsvc@carvercountymn.gov. Value, classification and homestead questions go to Property Assessment & Homesteading at (952) 361-1960 or assessment@carvercountymn.gov. Hours for the building are Monday through Friday, 8:00am to 4:30pm, closed on government holidays.

The county mails tax statements each year by March 31. Missing a statement does not excuse a late payment, a point the county's penalty page repeats in bold type.

sections.h2: When are Carver County property taxes due?
sections.html:
For most parcels the first half is due May 15 and the second half October 15. Most agricultural property pays its second half on November 15, and manufactured homes pay on August 31 and November 15. State law in Minn. Stat. 279.01 phrases the same dates as payment before May 16 and before October 16.

  • If the statement was not postmarked before April 25, the first half is due 21 days after the postmark date.
  • A parcel with $100 or less in tax pays the whole amount by the first-half date.
  • Class 4c seasonal recreational property not used commercially takes the homestead penalty schedule.
  • Second-half agricultural property pays no penalty if it is in by November 15.

There is only one statement. The second-half stub is on it, and the county does not mail another in the fall.

sections.h2: What does a late payment cost in Carver County?
sections.html:
Penalty starts the day after the due date and steps up on the first of each month. The county's schedule runs from 2% to 14%, and the numbers below are for a first-half payment on a residential parcel.

First-half penalty by payment date, Carver County residential property
Paid on or afterHomesteadNon-homestead
May 162%4%
June 14%8%
July 15%9%
August 16%10%
September 17%11%
October 18%12%
January 210%14%

Source: Carver County Penalty Rates page. First-half tax must be paid with its penalty before money counts toward the second half.

  • Only a U.S. Postal Service postmark on or before the due date counts. Private postage meter marks are rejected.
  • A bank bill-pay check usually carries no postmark, so it must arrive by the due date.
  • Online payments cannot come from a savings account, and a mistyped parcel number can delay a payment into penalty.

Minnesota also gives a one-time break: if a mailed payment is postmarked within one business day after the due date and the owner has not used the break before, the treasurer must abate the penalty (279.01, subd. 2).

sections.h2: How do I contest my Carver County valuation?
sections.html:
Start with a call to the assessor. The county lists four steps: contact the assessment office, go to an open book session or the local board of appeal and equalization, go to the county board, and then Minnesota Tax Court. You may file with the Tax Court directly at any point.

  1. January 2: every parcel is valued as of this date. The 2026 valuation, used for taxes payable in 2027, rests on sales from October 1, 2024 through September 30, 2025.
  2. March: the tax statement and the Notice of Valuation and Classification arrive together.
  3. April and May: local boards meet. State law sets those meetings between April 1 and May 31, and each board must finish within 20 days (Minn. Stat. 274.01). A board may not cut the assessor's total by more than one percent.
  4. June: the county board meets. You can appear only if you attended the local board, and you need an appointment made before June 1.
  5. April 30: Tax Court filing deadline. The 2026 date has passed, so the next one for the 2026 valuation is April 30, 2027.

In November every city, township, school district and the county hold Truth in Taxation meetings. Their notices show this year's tax and an estimate for the following year.

sections.h2: How do I pay Carver County property tax?
sections.html:
The county takes mailed checks, bank bill pay and an online payment system, and its penalty page gives the pitfalls to avoid. A check mailed on the due date needs a U.S. postmark from that day, and a bill-pay payment is on time only if it reaches the county by the due date. Re-enter the parcel number carefully, since a keying error can push a payment past the deadline. The payment portal does not accept a savings account.

Mortgage escrow is the other route: if your lender pays from escrow, the lender handles the due dates, but the owner of record still carries responsibility for confirming the bill was paid. Call (952) 361-1910 with questions about what is owed or how penalty is calculated.

sections.h2: What changes for property tax when a Carver County house sells?
sections.html:
Check the closing papers for who pays the year's tax, and confirm the full year is paid. The county's public access page shows statement copies and offers email reminders. For a payoff figure on anything past due, call (952) 361-1910.

Homestead status does not travel with the house. A new owner, a move into a trust, a name change or an owner added or removed each requires a new application to the assessor. Under 272.115 the assessor drops the homestead classification for the next assessment year after a sale unless the buyer applies and qualifies, and a buyer cannot be classed homestead if no certificate of value was filed. A qualifying owner may get the homestead market value exclusion, which lowers taxable value.

A seller whose taxes are behind can still sell. Ask the closing agent to request the amount due from the property tax office before the closing date, since penalty grows on the first of each month.

sections.h2: What does Carver County look like for a seller?
sections.html:
Carver County covers 354 square miles of land, which makes it Minnesota's second-smallest county by that measure. Its population went from 91,042 in 2010 to 106,922 in 2020, and the Census estimate for July 2025 is 114,379. Chaska is the seat and the largest city. Chanhassen lies partly in Hennepin County, so confirm which county bills a Chanhassen parcel before you call.

  • Median owner-occupied home value, 2020 to 2024: $453,600
  • Households: 41,175, with 2.65 people each
  • Median household income: $125,946
  • Housing units, July 2025: 44,930

At the median value, each 1% of assessed value is about $4,536, so the March notice is worth reading line by line. Cities such as Chaska, Waconia and Victoria and townships such as Laketown, Camden and Benton each run their own local board, and the date for yours is printed on the notice.

faqs.q: When is the first-half tax due in Carver County?
faqs.a: May 15 for most properties. If the statement was mailed after April 24, the due date is 21 days after the postmark. The second half is due October 15, or November 15 for most agricultural land.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Carver County property value?
faqs.a: Call the Carver County assessor at (952) 361-1960 or write to assessment@carvercountymn.gov. The assessor can explain the valuation notice and tell you the board dates for your city or township.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal my 2026 Carver County value?
faqs.a: The local and county board windows for 2026 and the April 30, 2026 Tax Court deadline have passed. Valuation notices for the next cycle arrive in March, and the next Tax Court filing deadline is April 30, 2027.

faqs.q: What if I mail my Carver County tax payment late?
faqs.a: Penalty applies from the day after the due date. If the envelope carries a U.S. postmark within one business day of the deadline and you have never used the abatement before, state law lets the treasurer waive it.

faqs.q: Does the buyer keep my homestead on a Carver County house?
faqs.a: No. The assessor removes the homestead classification for the following assessment year unless the buyer files a homestead application and qualifies. The buyer applies through the assessor's office.
